conventions: TypeScript strict; Prettier 2.6 (@excalidraw/prettier-config) enforced through eslint-plugin-prettier: 2-space indent, double quotes, trailing commas, 80-column wrap; the eslint fix command reformats, so long import lists wrap one name per line.

Import groups, blank line between groups: react and other externals (react, vitest), then @excalidraw/* value imports, then import type from @excalidraw/*, then relative imports (parent before sibling), then the scss side-effect import, then relative import type. Names inside one import are sorted case-insensitively.
Type-only imports use a separate `import type` statement (consistent-type-imports); never import jotai directly, use ../editor-jotai.

Utilities in packages/common/src are exported `const` arrow functions next to related helpers; private helpers are unexported `const` arrows; use `const`, `?.` and `??`; no `any` (a test may cast a stub with `as unknown as T`).
Theme checks compare against THEME.DARK / THEME.LIGHT from @excalidraw/common, never string literals.
Colour strings in code and tests are lowercase hex (#rrggbb, #rrggbbaa when alpha < 1).

Tests: vitest with globals (describe/it/expect/afterEach); `vi` is imported explicitly with `import { vi } from "vitest";`; editor tests render the full <Excalidraw /> through ./test-utils `render`, read state through `const { h } = window;`, build elements with `API` from ./helpers/api and drive input with `Keyboard` from ./helpers/ui and `fireEvent` from ./test-utils.
Never edit or regenerate __snapshots__ files; existing applyDarkModeFilter tests and the palette snapshot must stay green unchanged.
Comments are short English sentences explaining why, not what; no TODOs.

decisions.topic: Name and signature of the inverse
decisions.choice: export const revertDarkModeFilter = (color: string, enable = true): string, in packages/common/src/colors.ts directly after applyDarkModeFilter, reached through the existing `export * from "./colors"` of @excalidraw/common.
rejected: invertDarkModeFilter (reads as applying an invert filter)
decisions.reason: Mirrors applyDarkModeFilter's signature (same enable flag, same string-in hex-out contract) so call sites read symmetrically.

decisions.choice: Undo the steps in reverse order: first the existing cssHueRotate(r, g, b, -180 as Degrees) (hue-rotate(180deg) is its own inverse in the CSS matrix), then the exact algebraic inverse of cssInvert at 93%: Math.round(clamp((c - 255 * p) / (1 - 2 * p), 0, 255)) with p = clamp(percent, 0, 100) / 100; alpha copied from the input through rgbToHex like applyDarkModeFilter.
rejected: brute-force preimage search over the RGB cube (too slow on the per-pointermove path)
decisions.reason: A general closed-form inverse round-trips every colour the forward transform does not clamp, costs one tinycolor parse, and matches the measured values the test pins.

decisions.choice: No cache; DARK_MODE_COLORS_CACHE, cssInvert, cssHueRotate and applyDarkModeFilter stay byte-for-byte unchanged.
rejected: a second module-level Map keyed by picked colour
decisions.reason: Picked pixels are arbitrary (images, gradients, antialiasing) so a cache grows without bound, and NFR-1 forbids touching the forward cache.

decisions.choice: export const matchDarkModeColor = (pickedColor: string, sceneColors: Iterable<string>): string | null in colors.ts directly after revertDarkModeFilter: it returns the first candidate c, scene colours first in iteration order and then the palette (COLOR_PALETTE black, white, then each family's shades in object order; transparent excluded), whose applyDarkModeFilter(c).slice(0, 7) equals pickedColor.toLowerCase().slice(0, 7) (alpha ignored on both sides), returning c verbatim; candidates that are transparent or not a valid colour are skipped; null when nothing matches. getCurrentColor in dark theme returns matchDarkModeColor(color, sceneColors) ?? revertDarkModeFilter(color).
rejected: a hard-coded table of the 13 clamped colours
matching inside revertDarkModeFilter (keeps the inverse pure and scene-free)
decisions.reason: The 13 clamped palette colours (yellows among them) cannot be recovered by any inverse; an exact forward match against colours the user can actually have drawn recovers them exactly, and the inverse stays the fallback for arbitrary pixels.

decisions.choice: Built once per eyedropper effect run in EyeDropper.tsx, only in dark theme: a Set<string> of strokeColor and backgroundColor of stableProps.app.scene.getNonDeletedElements(), in element order; not rebuilt per pointermove.
rejected: rebuilding from the scene on every pointermove (O(elements) on the per-move path, NFR-3)
decisions.reason: Keeps the per-move cost to a Set walk of distinct colours plus cached applyDarkModeFilter lookups.

decisions.choice: Once, inside EyeDropper.tsx getCurrentColor (exact match first, inverse as fallback), when appState.theme === THEME.DARK; every consumer (LayerUI onChange preview, App.openEyeDropper onSelect, ColorInput's eyedropper, App.bucketFill temporary eyedropper and therefore App.cursor's bucket-fill cursor and actionChangeBucketFillBackgroundColor) receives the already-reverted colour, so actionProperties.tsx, App.bucketFill.ts and App.cursor.ts need no edit.
rejected: reverting in each consumer (four call sites, two of them in LayerUI.tsx/App.tsx/ColorInput.tsx outside the allowlist, and a double-revert risk)
reverting in the bucket-fill and cursor code as well (applies the inverse twice, violating FR-5)
decisions.reason: getCurrentColor is the single point where a canvas pixel becomes a colour, so applying the inverse there guarantees exactly-once for every user.

decisions.choice: The preview div keeps `style.background = currentColor` (now the reverted colour); its existing CSS `filter: var(--theme-filter)` re-applies the dark transform, so the swatch shows what the canvas shows. No scss change.
decisions.reason: Before the fix the swatch double-transformed the pixel; the fix makes it correct for free.

decisions.choice: ±1 per RGB channel, constant ROUND_TRIP_TOLERANCE = 1, never widened; 13 palette colours whose forward hue-rotate clamps are listed by name and hex with their measured round-trip hex and signed per-channel error (round trip minus original), asserted exactly.
decisions.reason: FR-2 / AC-1 fix this shape; the clamped colours are not injective under the forward transform, so no inverse can recover them; the eyedropper recovers them through matchDarkModeColor instead, and the exceptions test stays unchanged.

decisions.topic: Feeding a pixel to the eyedropper in jsdom
decisions.choice: After render, vi.spyOn(h.app.canvas.getContext("2d")!, "getImageData") returning `{ data: Uint8ClampedArray.from([r, g, b, 255]) } as unknown as ImageData`; vitest-canvas-mock returns the same context object for the same canvas, which is the one EyeDropper reads.
rejected: drawing on the mock canvas (vitest-canvas-mock always returns zeroed pixels)
decisions.reason: Deterministic pixel value independent of the mock renderer.

decisions.choice: Re-export revertDarkModeFilter from packages/excalidraw/index.tsx in the same import and export statements as applyDarkModeFilter, and add a `### Fixes` entry under `## Unreleased` in packages/excalidraw/CHANGELOG.md.
decisions.reason: applyDarkModeFilter is public there, so hosts that use it to render get its inverse alongside; matchDarkModeColor stays internal (exported from @excalidraw/common only, not re-exported from index.tsx).
